images.title: Two numbers, one nearest hundred
images.purpose: Show that two different numbers on either side of a hundred both have that hundred as their nearest hundred.
images.composition: One road from 5,300 to 5,500 with a carrot at each end and one in the middle, two rabbits near the middle carrot, short jump arrows above the road to the middle carrot and grey brackets below for the far carrots.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas with one horizontal road across the middle: a thick flat bar in #2B2B2B spanning most of the width, with an equal margin at the left and right. Exactly 5 tick marks on the road, for the numbers: 5,300 at the left end, 5,380 two fifths of the way along, 5,400 at the exact middle, 5,420 three fifths of the way along, 5,500 at the right end. A carrot (amber #E69F00, green #009E73 leaf) stands at the left end, at the middle and at the right end: 3 carrots. Two flat grey rabbits sit on the road: one at the 5,380 tick and one at the 5,420 tick, both facing the middle carrot. The number labels sit just under the road, under their ticks: 5,300, 5,380, 5,400, 5,420, 5,500. ABOVE the road: two teal #0072B2 arcs, each with an arrowhead pointing at the middle carrot, one from the left rabbit and one from the right rabbit, each with the text 20 jumps above it. UNDER the number labels: two thin grey #6B7280 brackets, one from the 5,380 tick to the 5,300 tick and one from the 5,420 tick to the 5,500 tick, each with the text 80 jumps under it. The middle carrot has a #CC79A7 ring and the tag same nearest hundred above the road over it. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Numbers on both sides of a hundred can share that hundred as their nearest hundred.
images.description: The numbers 5,380 and 5,420 each need 20 jumps to 5,400 and 80 jumps to the far hundreds, so both have the nearest hundred 5,400.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's idea of numbers that share a nearest number, shown on a number line. The numbers are the plan's own from part (a) of the concept's worked example: 5,380 and 5,420 with nearest hundred 5,400. The label 20 jumps and the label 80 jumps are each printed twice. The part with 7,997 and 8,002 is not drawn.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which carrot each rabbit would pick, then count the jumps. Point out that one rabbit is below 5,400 and one above it, yet they pick the same carrot. Misconception M_NEAR_FAR.

image_decisions.why: One road with two rabbits on either side of the same carrot shows what it means to share a nearest number.
